builder_notes.pattern: DialogTrigger controlled open/close requires isOpen-aware stub in jsdom
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: DialogTrigger with isOpen={showEndConfirm} — simple children pass-through stub always renders AlertDialog, causing 'dialog initially absent' assertions to fail
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Stub DialogTrigger to render childArray.slice(0, 1) when !isOpen; render all children when isOpen. Treats children[0] as the trigger element and children[1] as the dialog.
builder_notes.stack_example: HeadToHeadPage.test.tsx DialogTrigger stub: const childArray = React.Children.toArray(children); return isOpen ? childArray : childArray.slice(0, 1)

builder_notes.pattern: react-aria-components Button needs its own stub separate from @react-spectrum/s2 Button
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: import { Button as AriaButton } from 'react-aria-components' alongside S2 components — two distinct Button implementations in the same page
builder_notes.stack_example: HeadToHeadPage uses AriaButton for ComparisonCard (keyboard-accessible clickable card) and S2 Button for action buttons — both need onPress-to-onClick mapping

builder_notes.pattern: Multi-value stat cards cause getByText ambiguity — use getAllByText or target-adjacent label
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: AnalyticsPage (and similar) renders multiple stat cards where numeric values can collide (3 Total Items, 3 Total Tiers)
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Use getAllByText('3') to get all matches; assert count >= 1. Or target the adjacent label directly: screen.getByText('Total Items').
builder_notes.stack_example: AnalyticsPage.test.tsx: screen.getAllByText('3').length >= 1 avoids the 'multiple elements found' error from getByText

narrative: Good app, place but not win.
